_comment: Per-chart narratives. CI (build_prompt.py -> GitHub Models -> write_narrative.py) overwrites these from live numbers; this committed copy is the fallback so the page always reads well. source = 'fallback' | 'github-models'.

notes.basket: The breakfast basket, an average of coffee, sugar, wheat, and orange juice prices indexed to 2015 (=100), stands at 132, reflecting a 32% increase since that baseline year. This headline rise reflects a climb that is uneven across components and has primarily occurred more recently. The index signifies that, on average, prices for this selection of common breakfast commodities have outpaced general inflation since 2015. These are global prices sourced from FRED and IMF data.
notes.movers: Coffee is the main driver with a 93% increase since 2015, followed by orange juice at 22%, while wheat and sugar have seen more modest rises of 7% and 5% respectively. These shifts are largely the result of weather and crop disease factors, such as frost, drought in coffee-growing arabica regions, and citrus greening and hurricanes affecting orange juice. These soft commodities trade in relatively thin markets, meaning supply shocks from localized events can cause disproportionate price swings rather than broad economic inflation.
notes.why: The overall rise is therefore concentrated in a few weather-sensitive crops rather than a generalized commodity price trend. Due to the nature of their markets and agricultural cycles, prices for these inputs can remain elevated for several years following adverse growing conditions.
